newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina plans fewer, but bigger bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Argentina plans fewer, but bigger bond issues.

text.p: Argentina's undersecretary of finance Miguel Kiguel said in an interview published Thursday that Argentina plans to set fewer, but larger bond issues in the future.
Kiguel told business daily Ambito Financiero the financing strategy for the years to come is to "issue less paper, especially in marks, yens and dollars, but with bigger amounts."

The government has targeted $8.5 billion of debt to be placed overseas this year, of which it placed $2 billion in December and announced $2 billion for the second half of this month and another $1 billion for March.
Apart from overseas placements, the undersecretary said the government also plans $3.5 billion of debt issues for the local market.

That implies only 30 percent of the debt to be issued will be placed in the local market, but Kiguel said by 2000 this will be reversed, with between 50 and 70 percent of debt to be placed in Argentina mainly through Treasury bonds.

"The intention is that before the end of the year, we will issue local Treasury bonds with five-year maturities," he said. Argentina launched its new local Treasury bond program in December with a $500 million two-year issue.

Kiguel added that he expects about 85 percent of the 20-year global bond issue announced Tuesday will be placed with U.S. insurance companies, mutual funds and other funds that invest in Latin American paper.

Economy Minister Roque Fernandez announced Tuesday a two-tranche, $2.0 billion global bond split between a five- and a 20-year issue. Kiguel said it was not yet decided what amount will be placed at each maturity.
He said between 70 and 80 percent of the five-year issue will be placed with European and Asian wholesale investors and the rest with U.S. investors.
Kiguel added the other $1.0 billion bond announced by Fernandez to be issued before the end of March will probably be denominated in a European currency in two or three placements.
